content:
matt: Heads-up — getting a few support tickets about the analytics sidepanel 'Slim mode' quick-save. Users say filters vanish when they switch routes. Anyone seen this?
anya: I thought saved views were per-route by default. Can you paste repro steps?
sam: Repro: open sidepanel on /routes/ingest -> set model filter to 'gpt-3.5' -> quicksave -> switch to /routes/transform -> switch back to /routes/ingest -> filters reset. Quicksave seems to create a global saved view instead of a route-scoped one.
liz: That's unexpected. We committed to per-route savedqueries in the roadmap. Where does the API define scope currently? cc @chris
chris: The current SavedView model only has scope enum: GLOBAL | ORG | PROJECT. No ROUTE or MODEL. We kind of punted earlier and used folder-level scoping. PR reference: https://git.company/repo/pull/1234
matt: So the quicksave flow probably defaults to GLOBAL when invoked from sidepanel. We should either infer scope from context (route + model) or make the UI prompt users.
anya: Proposal: default to ROUTE if sidepanel.context.route exists, include optional model_name. Fallback to GLOBAL only if no context. Need API + UX changes.
sam: Telemetry note: we currently don't record where saves originate. Add metric savedview.create.source with values like 'sidepanel'|'route-header'|'api' and savedview.create.scope (inferred vs explicit).
liz: Also think about quotas — global saved views count differently. If we create lots of per-route saves automatically, orgs might hit saved-view quotas unintentionally. Need to surface that.
chris: API plan: add scope enum values ROUTE and MODEL, and optional fields route_id and model_name. Keep backwards-compat: missing fields imply GLOBAL. UI should expose a minimal 'Scope' chip during quicksave to let users override.
anya: Quick mock: quicksave modal shows a secondary row under name: "Scope: Route /ingest · Model: llama-2" small chevron to change -> opens compact scope picker. Default is inferred.
matt: Can we soft-roll this? Start with auto-infer on canary and record inferred_scope telemetry, then surface UI after a few weeks. Ops: @ops-runbooks any concerns with a gradual rollout?
ops-runbooks: We can feature-flag it. Note migrations: existing GLOBAL saved views won't be automatically reclassified; changing defaults only affects new saves. If we want to migrate historical views, we need a migration plan and product approval.
sam: For telemetry schema I'll propose event savedview.create with properties {inferred_scope, explicit_scope, source, route_id?, model_name?}. Will draft in infra-tracking board.
liz: Also update console docs and SDK docs so customers understand the difference between per-route and global views. Product copy should call out quota semantics.
matt: Action items: 1) API PR adding scope + fields (chris), 2) Telemetry event draft (sam), 3) UI mock + minimal opt-out flow (anya), 4) Ops migration/runbook (ops-runbooks). Target: canary next Tues. Everyone +1?
chris: +1 — will start PR today.
anya: :thumbsup: I'll drop mocks in #design later this afternoon.
sam: I'll ping infra for instrumentation and land telemetry draft by EOD.
ops-runbooks: I'll create a runbook entry and migration notes, link back here.
product-bot: DeployBot: feature flag 'sidepanel-scope-v1' created and tied to matts-team-canary.
matt: Thanks — if anyone hits edgecases (eg filters that shouldn't be per-route like global time-range presets), drop them here and we'll handle exceptions.
